slot.brief: Convex/mirror problem: object at given distance, image formed on screen; use mirror formula and magnification to find focal length and image nature (two equations two unknowns).

stem: A $3\ \text{cm}$ tall object is placed $30\ \text{cm}$ in front of a concave mirror. A sharp image on a screen is $6\ \text{cm}$ tall. What are the mirror's focal length and the image nature?
options: $20\ \text{cm}$; real, inverted, twice the object size
$15\ \text{cm}$; real, inverted, twice the object size
$20\ \text{cm}$; real, upright, twice the object size
$40\ \text{cm}$; virtual, upright, twice the object size

verdicts.working: Image magnification has magnitude 6/3 = 2. A sharp image on a screen is real and, for a concave mirror, inverted. With u = -30 cm, m = -v/u = -2 gives v = -60 cm. Then 1/f = 1/u + 1/v = -1/20 cm⁻¹, so the focal-length magnitude is 20 cm.

working:
$|m|=h_i/h_o=6/3=2$, so $|v|=2u=60\ \text{cm}$. $\dfrac{1}{f}=\dfrac{1}{30}+\dfrac{1}{60}$, hence $f=20\ \text{cm}$. A real image is inverted.

Independent check: Image magnification has magnitude 6/3 = 2. A sharp image on a screen is real and, for a concave mirror, inverted. With u = -30 cm, m = -v/u = -2 gives v = -60 cm. Then 1/f = 1/u + 1/v = -1/20 cm⁻¹, so the focal-length magnitude is 20 cm.
solution:
The magnification magnitude is $|m|=h_i/h_o=6/3=2$, so the image distance has magnitude $|v|=2(30)=60\ \text{cm}$. A sharp image on a screen is real and inverted.
$$\frac{1}{f}=\frac{1}{30}+\frac{1}{60}=\frac{1}{20}\quad\Rightarrow\quad f=20\ \text{cm}$$
